title: Festivals
objective: After this level you can describe music festivals from Woodstock onward.
summary: Woodstock (1969) drew about 400,000 to a farm in Bethel, New York, most without tickets, and ended with Hendrix's anthem. Live Aid (1985) linked London and Philadelphia for famine relief.

cards.headline: The Woodstock festival didn't happen in Woodstock.
cards.body: Woodstock ran August 15–18, 1969, on Max Yasgur's farm in Bethel, New York. The organizers kept the Woodstock name anyway. About 400,000 people showed up. What happens when that many people come to hear music in one field?

cards.headline: Mud, gate-crashers and a movie
cards.body: Not what anyone planned. Security was so thin that most people got in without paying, and rain turned the field to mud. The festival nearly bankrupted its four inexperienced promoters. What rescued them was a film: Michael Wadleigh's 1970 documentary was a commercial success that recouped their losses. The festival lost money; the movie of the festival made it back.

cards.headline: 9 a.m. Monday: Hendrix plays the anthem
cards.body: Jimi Hendrix didn't take the stage until around 9 a.m. on Monday, August 18, by which time many festivalgoers had already left. His "Star-Spangled Banner" used the electric guitar to act out the words: rockets and bombs bursting, a siren-like wail. Musicians call this text painting, music that paints what the lyrics say.

cards.headline: From one field to the whole planet
cards.body: Sixteen years later, a festival didn't even need a single field. Live Aid, on July 13, 1985, ran at the same time at Wembley Stadium in London and JFK Stadium in Philadelphia, raising money for famine relief in Ethiopia, and it was broadcast worldwide. The audience was no longer just the people standing in front of the stage.

questions.prompt: Where did the 1969 Woodstock festival actually take place?

options.label: In the town of Woodstock, New York
options.rationale: The organizers kept the name, but not the town.

options.label: On Max Yasgur's farm in Bethel, New York
In JFK Stadium, Philadelphia
options.rationale: That was Live Aid's American stage, in 1985.

questions.explanation: Woodstock ran August 15–18, 1969, on Max Yasgur's farm in Bethel, New York.

questions.prompt: About 400,000 people came to Woodstock. Why did it still nearly bankrupt its promoters?

options.label: The bands refused to play in the rain
options.rationale: The music went on through the mud.

options.label: A law made the tickets free
options.rationale: No law did; thin security did.

options.label: Hardly anyone came because of the rain
Most people got in without paying

questions.explanation: With little security, most of the crowd walked in free. The 1970 documentary film later recouped the losses.

questions.prompt: Hendrix's anthem acted out rockets and bombs. Which technique from Level 28's madrigals does that match?

options.label: Rubato, stretching and hurrying the beats
options.rationale: Rubato bends time; Hendrix was acting out words.

options.label: A leitmotif tied to one character
options.rationale: A leitmotif labels a character; this painted the words.

options.label: Word painting, as in Weelkes' descending notes
Basso continuo, a bass with improvised chords
options.rationale: That's a Baroque accompaniment, not acting out a text.

questions.explanation: Hendrix's guitar acted out the anthem's words, just as madrigal word painting makes the notes descend on "descending".
